requirement:
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.

A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
rationale:
**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: I found no test-adequacy gap in `requirements.authoring.reassessment`. All five supplied tests carry a `{test}` reference to it. I did not read the implementation or the test server behaviors, and I judged the tests only from the supplied source.

Obligation-to-test mapping:

- **Freshness check after a round's additions, and reassessing a subject whose corrections were all satisfied when its inputs changed.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[corrections_replay_reference_only_mixed_and_regression_findings]` has a "reference-only" case. A failed assessment is applied, reassessed and fails again, is applied again, then reassessed to success. The test asserts `determination == true`, the `(applied)` output and the exact marker placement in the source.
  - The "confirm-reassessment" case runs the reassessment under `--policy confirm` and asserts the reassessment succeeds. It checks that a fresh success establishes `true`.
  - Other cases in the same test show a failure with an unread or unmatched item keeps `false`.
- **Reassessing other subjects made stale, including definitions, citation reviews and site reviews outside the initial selection.**
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[reference_edits_reassess_a_skipped_subject_sharing_the_changed_input]` covers a site review plus a requirement. After the edit it asserts that both `src/lib.rs fn[shared]` and `requirements.alpha` are reassessed, and that the evidence is `true` and the repository validates.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_named_reference_edit_refreshes_a_definition_and_a_citation_that_read_the_same_text]` covers a citation review on `notes.txt`. It asserts that each peer sharing the edited text is reassessed after the round, and that validation has no errors.
- **Independent reassessments run under the cited concurrency requirement.** The batch tests configure concurrency 2 and check the peers are reassessed together, matching order-insensitively. The limit itself belongs to `requirements.authoring.concurrency` and its own tests, so it is not reassessed here.
- **A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an unapplied action pauses for the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other subjects continue.**
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_changed_shared_input_does_not_resume_a_paused_subject]` covers both pause causes, a manual instruction and an unreachable or unapplied action.
  - It asserts the paused `alpha` is assessed exactly twice and stays `false`, even though a shared input changed.
  - It asserts `beta` is assessed three times, ends `true`, and has its marker applied, so other subjects continue.
  - The "mixed" and "new-regression" cases in `corrections_replay_reference_only_mixed_and_regression_findings` assert the "paused for manual work" output. They also assert that applied markers are written alongside the manual instruction and that the result stays `false`.
- **An already-present marker or stale selector alone causes no reassessment, and the negative judgment stands when inputs are unchanged.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stale_and_already_present_references_do_not_retry_unchanged_inputs]` runs both variants. It asserts exactly two model requests, so there is no retry.
  - It asserts the source is unchanged, or holds only the externally changed text when stale, and that the "item changed since assessment" message appears only in the stale variant.
  - It asserts `determination == false` and that the observed input is recorded.
  - The "anchor" case in the corrections test also asserts the "already present" output and no further assessment.
- **Repeating while eligible subjects remain, with no limit on rounds.** The "reference-only" case runs more than one correction round followed by reassessment. The batch tests run several rounds across subjects. A test of a very large round count would only repeat the same loop, and the requirement names no boundary.
- **`--stdout` reports the assessment and proposed corrections without editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.** The "stdout" case asserts the evidence file is unchanged. It asserts the proposed correction is printed and nothing is `(applied)`. It asserts the source has zero markers and that exactly the two scripted requests were made.
- **Fresh inputs and the selected policy.** The stale variant checks that inputs are re-observed. The confirm-policy case checks the policy is used on reassessment.

Second assessment `false`: Add a reassessment test that checks the concurrency clause: "Independent reassessments MUST run under `requirements.authoring.concurrency`". Use a fixture where one edit makes at least three independent subjects stale, such as the requirement, citation review and site review peers in `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[a_named_reference_edit_refreshes_a_definition_and_a_citation_that_read_the_same_text]`. Configure `concurrency` to 2. Have the fake server hold the reassessment requests. For example, use `require_overlap`, a barrier like `Behavior::WarmupBarrier`, or the recorded `peak`/`timeline`. Assert that at least two reassessments overlap and that the peak number of simultaneous requests never exceeds the configured concurrency. — The reassessment tests call `Server::start_with(false, ...)`, so no overlap is required. None of them checks the peak count of simultaneous assessments or the timeline of the reassessment round. `reference_edits_reassess_a_skipped_subject_sharing_the_changed_input` and `a_named_reference_edit_refreshes_a_definition_and_a_citation_that_read_the_same_text` only check which subjects were reassessed. Both would pass if the reassessment round ran sequentially, ignoring `concurrency`. They would also pass if it ran unbounded and exceeded the configured limit. Both behaviors violate the clause that independent reassessments run under `requirements.authoring.concurrency`.

Recorded the second assessment (`false`).

Each named authoring configuration MUST accept an optional positive integer
`concurrency` in its configuration table. When omitted, the maximum number of
simultaneous assessments MUST default to the number of available logical CPUs
for Bedrock and OpenAI, falling back to one when that count is unavailable, and to one for

MUST be rejected as invalid configuration.
Batch authoring MUST use asynchronous tasks on a runtime with a fixed worker
thread pool. The number of assessments running at once MUST NOT exceed the
selected concurrency. Each assessment MUST retain its own model conversation and
usage record. Transient provider failures, including throttling, MUST be
retried within the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`; every other provider error MUST
be reported through the ordinary assessment-failure path.
